free_tier.stated: No free tier and no trial on the pages read: "Only $8.99 USD / Month per IP" and "No contracts - Cancel anytime - Rapid activation".

interface_detail: Configuration file plus a dashboard; the docs have a page titled "Create API Key", but the API itself was not read.
tooling: wg-quick on Linux, the vendor's Windows client, a Docker image
chaining: Put it on a free-tier VM and the VM gains a stable ingress address without an elastic IP; reverse DNS is included, so a mail listener is possible on port 25.
binding_note: Nothing is documented, so the first wall at 1 TiB/month is an unpublished the provider judgement rather than a counter the client can watch. That is worse than a number: capacity cannot be planned against a clause.

identity_cost.detail: "Your payment method will be charged without further action from you until you cancel" (refund policy). The sign-up form was not read, so card-versus-other is inferred from a paid monthly subscription rather than observed.

reliability_note: The vendor recommends its own watchdog script because an ISP address change can hang the handshake; the address itself is static across ISP changes.
confidence_note: Price, ports, protocol and the configuration file are read from first-party pages. Volume is the open field: a support reply or a pricing-page transfer figure would settle it.

evidence.proved: USD 8.99 per IP per month; dedicated IPv4 and IPv6; no bandwidth figure on the page
the vendor issues pi0.conf, imported with wg-quick, then ports are opened on the server's own firewall
"All ports and protocols, with port ranges"; "All: TCP, UDP, ICMP"; 32 locations; port mapping is done in the dashboard

notes: Port mapping is done in the dashboard as single ports or ranges ("Map single ports or ranges in the dashboard, with optional source-IP rules"), and the page does not state a maximum count, so treat the port count as unverified. A third-party table by competitor GetAStatic lists "Any port you open" at $8.99, which agrees on price and ports but adds nothing on volume.

extras.wg_detail: "Download the Linux configuration from your IP address. Copy the pi0.conf to /etc/wireguard/" then "systemctl start wg-quick@pi0". The address is a whole IPv4 plus a public IPv6: "Every IP includes both a public IPv4 and a public IPv6 address, routed through the same tunnel."
extras.transit_note: The vendor carries the traffic through its own edge and, it says, does not inspect it: "We never inspect or modify your packets".
